name: Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon (33rd ed.)
short_description: The 33rd Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon was held in Pattaya, Chonburi, Thailand, with the 10 km and 4.5 km races on 26 September 2026 and the marathon and half marathon on 27 September.
ai_summary: The 33rd Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon, organised by Thailand Tri-League, started and finished at Terminal 21 Pattaya on North Pattaya Road in Chonburi, Thailand. The 10 km, 4.5 km wheelchair race and 4.5 km family run were on Saturday 26 September 2026, and the marathon (3.30am start, seven-hour limit) and half marathon (5.10am) on Sunday 27 September. The race moved from July to September in 2026 after a procurement delay, and drew 21,727 entrants from 58 countries.
pros: Fully closed roads on race morning, with a finish along Pattaya Beach Road
Low entry fee: 800 to 950 baht for the marathon in 2026
Drinks about every 2 km and a seven-hour marathon limit
Shallow field: 2:54 was tenth among men in 2026, with Thai and age-group prize money
cons: Saturated air: 27°C and 100% humidity at the 3.30am start in 2026
Rolling roads, with Thappraya Road crossed twice and no published elevation profile
The date moved from July in 2025 to late September in 2026
Five intermediate cut-offs before the seven-hour limit, and a 3.30am start

excerpt_quotes.quote: The weather was extremely hot. Even with wind from the beach, it was still very humid
excerpt_quotes.attribution: Lodkeo Inthakoumman, half-marathon winner, quoted in Laotian Times

research_highlights: The 2026 edition was moved from July (the 2025 race was on 19-20 July) to 26-27 September after Pattaya's procurement process for the organiser was delayed; the marathon started at 3.30am and rain fell through both race mornings, according to local reports.
Course starts and finishes at Terminal 21 Pattaya, running through Jomtien Beach Road, Sukhumvit highway, and Pattaya Beach Front Road with a mix of flat and rolling terrain
The marathon had 22 drink stations, roughly every 2km, with bananas at seven of them and a 'Hit the Wall' station near 32km; the half marathon had 12 stations.
The organisers cite 20,250 entrants in 2025, and 21,727 entrants from 58 countries were reported for 2026, about 10,964 on Saturday and 10,763 on Sunday.
The marathon, half marathon and 10km courses carried a World Athletics Road Race Label for 2026.
research_watchouts: Heat and humidity are a known challenge: the 2025 half-marathon winner, Lodkeo Inthakoumman, said the weather was extremely hot and very humid even with wind from the beach.
After the beach section the course turns rolling, with flat stretches alternating with gradual rises, which the organiser calls the key test of the route.
Runners starting more than 15 minutes after the gun are disqualified, and entry fees are not refunded in any case.

faqs.question: When is the Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon held?
faqs.answer: The 33rd edition was held over the weekend of 26 and 27 September 2026. The 10 km and both 4.5 km races were on Saturday 26 September, and the marathon and half marathon on Sunday 27 September, starting at 3.30am and 5.10am. The 2025 race had been held in July.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at this event?
faqs.answer: Five races over four distances: a 42.195 km marathon, a 21.1 km half marathon, a 10 km, a 4.5 km wheelchair race and a 4.5 km family run. Cut-offs were seven hours for the marathon, three and a half hours for the half and two hours for the 10 km.

faqs.question: Where does the race take place?
faqs.answer: In Pattaya, Chonburi, about 147 km from Bangkok. All races started and finished at Terminal 21 Pattaya on North Pattaya Road. The marathon ran along Pattaya Beach Road, over Thappraya Road to Jomtien, out and back on Sukhumvit Road, then back along Jomtien Beach; roads were closed from midnight to 11am.
